question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Initial British naval operations and bases during the First Carnatic War]
options: Fort St. George — Main British stronghold and seat of Madras Presidency captured by the French in 1746
Fort St. David — British coastal fortress at Cuddalore that became the temporary British headquarters after Madras fell
Calcutta (Fort William) — British settlement in Bengal from which Admiral Griffin's squadron received reinforcements
Goa — The naval base from which Commodore Barnet launched the initial British attack on French ships in 1745
wrong_fact: Commodore Barnet's squadron did not launch attacks from Goa. Goa was a Portuguese colony. Barnet's squadron operated from British bases and patrol stations in the Indian Ocean, utilizing Madras and Calcutta as their primary hubs.
explanation: At the start of the conflict, Commodore Barnet's English squadron seized French merchantmen. The English Presidency was centered at Fort St. George in Madras. After Madras fell to the French in 1746, the British administration shifted south to Fort St. David at Cuddalore. Reinforcements and naval support were coordinated with Fort William in Calcutta. Goa, a Portuguese enclave, played no part in British naval operations during this war.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British military movements and targets, 1746–1748]
options: Pondicherry — The French capital besieged by Admiral Boscawen's land and naval forces in 1748
Cuddalore — English settlement defended by Major Stringer Lawrence against French incursions
Tellicherry — The British factory on the Malabar Coast that launched a diversionary land attack on Mahé in 1747
Negapatam — Dutch settlement where Peyton's British squadron retreated after the naval battle with La Bourdonnais
wrong_fact: Tellicherry did not launch a land attack on Mahé in 1747. While Tellicherry (British) and Mahé (French) were close neighbors on the Malabar Coast, local chiefs and factors maintained a neutrality pact during the First Carnatic War to protect trade.
explanation: In 1748, Admiral Boscawen led a massive British siege of Pondicherry but failed to capture it. Major Stringer Lawrence successfully defended Cuddalore (Fort St. David) from French attacks. Following the naval clash off Negapatam, Peyton withdrew the British squadron, eventually sailing to Bengal. On the Malabar Coast, Tellicherry and Mahé factor officials agreed to remain neutral, so no British land attack on Mahé took place in 1747.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British strategic routes, naval coordination, and bases of support, c. 1745–1748]
options: Trincomalee — Strategic harbor in Ceylon where British warships sheltered during the monsoon season
St. Helena — Atlantic island base where the British fleet under Boscawen assembled before sailing to the East Indies
Devikottai — Fort at the mouth of the Coleroon River captured by the British in 1748 to secure a northern naval depot
Balasore — English factory in Odisha that supplied provisions to Peyton's retreating fleet in 1746
wrong_fact: Devikottai was not captured by the British in 1748 during the First Carnatic War. The British expedition to Devikottai (in Tanjore territory) occurred in 1749, after the war had ended, in support of a deposed claimant to the Tanjore throne.
explanation: During the war, British squadrons used Trincomalee in Ceylon (held by the Dutch) to refit and avoid monsoons. Admiral Boscawen's fleet assembled and refitted at key stopovers like St. Helena and the Cape of Good Hope. Balasore in Odisha was a vital supply link for English ships heading to Bengal. The capture of Devikottai occurred in 1749, after the signing of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, marking the onset of inter-war disputes.
